Noida-201301, Utter Pradesh and Anr. ....Petitioners.

Versus

Mr. Brijesh Kumar h/f.
Mr. N.S. Tekale, Advocate for petitioners.
Mr. S.G. Sangle, App for respondents.

Coram : T.V. Nalawade And
 Shrikant D. Kulkarni, Jj.
 Dated : 03/11/2020.
Order :

1. The petition is fled to challenge the order dated 20.7.2018 issued by Commissioner under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 to prohibit transportation of Gutkha and similar items under section 30(2)(a) of this Special Enactment.
It is contended that the order issued is illegal and void as the Commissioner has no power to impose ban on transportation.
The petitioner is manufacturer of articles including chewing tobacco and it has manufacturing unit at Noida, Utter Pradesh.
Both the sides are heard.
2. The petition is fled by manufacturing company through its General Manager and petitioner No. 2 appears to be a person who is in control of the things of the company.
It is their contention that on 18.12.2018 the consignment of product, of chewing product was being transported from Noida to purchaser from Bidar, Karnataka in a truck.
It is contended that on 22.12.2018 the truck was intercepted in Maharashtra, in Degloor Tahsil and the truck was taken by police to police station.

It is contended that on 24.12.2018 Food Safety Officer checked the contents of the truck and gave complaint to police that the transportation was in violation of prohibitory order issued under Food Safety and Standards Act and then crime came to be registered.
The contents of the truck came to be M/S Dharampal Premchand Ltd.

sentences.text: 3. It appears that in the past Criminal Application No. 250/2019 was fled in respect of the said action of the police and Food Safety Officer, but this Court dismissed the criminal application which was fled for quashing of the crime.

It appears that the truck was released by the learned J.M.F.C.,
but the goods were not released.

Even when the decision given by this Court in Criminal Application No. 250/2019 was challenged by fling Special Leave Petition (Criminal) Diary No(s).31844/2019 in Supreme Court and the said proceeding came to be dismissed, the present proceeding is fled.
4. It can be said that the previous proceeding, Criminal Application No. 250/2019 was fled for the company as the company would have been beneftted if the F.I.R. was quashed by this Court.
It was submitted that the company is not made accused though company ought to have made accused in such a case.
It is clear that the persons who were controlling the company were behind Criminal Application No. 250/2019 and now by taking the name of the company, they have fled the present proceeding.
Thus, the petitioners intend to reopen the matter which is decided by this Court on merits in the past.
5. The contentions made in the previous proceeding are quoted by this Court at para No. 4 and they are as under :-
" 4) The learned counsel for the applicant, driver of the truck, submitted that tobacco was being transported from Uttar Pradesh to Bidar, Karnataka.
He has produced tax invoices in respect of some of the materials which are shown to be seized.

He submitted that under the notifcation in question of the Commissioner of Food and Drugs Administration, Maharashtra State, though there is ban on manufacture,
storage, distribution, transportation or sale of tobacco which is either favoured,
sainted or mixed with any of the said adhesives under the provisions of section 30 (2)
(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act")
there could not have been prohibition on transportation.
He also submitted that in view of provisions of Articles 19, 301 and 304 of the Constitution of India, such prohibition order also could not have been issued.
Admittedly, these articles are banned in Maharashtra under the aforesaid notifcation for the aforesaid purposes.
The said notifcation is not challenged in the present proceeding and relief of only quashing of the F.I.R. is claimed."
The aforesaid contentions were considered by this Court.
This Court considered the submissions made by the learned APP and also the decision given in similar matters and those observations are at para Nos. 5 and 6.

They are as under :-
"5) The learned Additional Public Prosecutor has produced on record along with reply affidavit, the results of the examination of the samples showing that in all these samples nicotine was detected.

He submitted that the point raised is already decided by this Court in the cases like Writ Petition No.9865/2012 (M/s. Vishnu Pouch Packaging Private Limited v. The State of Maharashtra) decided on 1-2-2013, Writ M/S Dharampal Premchand Ltd. 6) Those proceedings were fled by the persons who were doing business of manufacture, supply and distribution of panmasala containing tobacco (popularly called as Gutkha) and panmasala containing other harmful substances like magnesium carbonate.
This Court referred to the decision of the Apex Court given in Criminal Appeal No.1195/2018 (State of Maharashtra & Others v. Sayyed Hassan) decided on 20-9-2018 and other decisions.

entities.text: Criminal Appeal No.1195/2018 (State of Maharashtra & Others v. Sayyed Hassan)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Writ Petition No.9865/2012 (cited supra) it was a case of a businessman that he was only transporting the material from Gujarat to Karnataka through Maharashtra and there was a challenge to the seizure of the goods and at that time there was notifcation dated 19-7-2012.
No licence was obtained under the Act as such substance is treated as food article.
It was held that there was contravention of the provisions of the Act in view of the Notifcation.
Provision of section 3 (n) of the Act was considered.

Defnition of "food business"
contains transportation and so relief in respect of seized Gutkha was refused.
In the subsequent decision viz. Writ Petition No.1631/2012 (cited supra) a Standing Order of 2012 was challenged.
The contentions that such transportation also cannot be prohibited under Articles 301 and 304 of the Constitution were considered and the prayer for stay of the notifcation was rejected.
The present notifcation is also on the same line.

A specifc word "transportation" is also there which is prohibited under the notifcation."
6)
Thus, the power of Commissioner to issue order under challenge was also challenged in the previous proceeding.
In the previous proceeding, this Court held that the point was already considered and decided by this Court at Principle Seat though it was embodied in diferent previous notifcation.

This decision was given in Writ Petition No. 9865/2012 decided on 1.2.2013 (M/s.
Vishnu Pouch Packaging Private Limited Vs. The State of Maharashtra and others).

entities.text: Vishnu Pouch Packaging Private Limited Vs. The State of Maharashtra and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has laid down that as the defnition of 'Food Business' given in section 3(n) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 includes transportation, for transportation of such articles licence needs to be obtained under section 31(1) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
This Court had refused to grant interim relief by making such observations.

While deciding Criminal Application No.
250/2019 this Court has laid down that the Commissioner has such power and so, the challenge raised in the present matter is already decided by this Court.

Which substances are covered under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is considered and law in that regard is laid down in the case reported as 2013 (2) Bom.C.R. 383 [Dhariwal Industries Limited and Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors.].

entities.text: 2013 (2) Bom.C.R. 383 [Dhariwal Industries Limited and Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors.]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The substance involved in the present matter like chewing tobacco is included as food product.
Further, other articles described as tobacco, Pan Masala containing tobacco etc. are also treated as food articles.

This Court considered the provision of Article 19 of Constitution of India in this reported case and also in the case of Vishnu Pouch Packaging Pvt. Ltd. cited supra.
7) The decision of Criminal Application No. 250/2019 was challenged in Supreme Court by Naushad s/o. Babu Khan and Anr., the person who probably controls the company.

The Supreme Court M/S Dharampal Premchand Ltd. Through ... vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others on 3 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114267583/

sentences.text: "UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following ORDER Permission to fle special leave petition is granted.
Delay condoned.
The special Leave Petition is dismissed.
Pending application(s) shall also stand disposed of."
8) The aforesaid circumstances show that the Special Leave Petition was entertained and then it was dismissed by the Supreme Court.
Thus, it is not open to the petitioner to open this point again.

Learned counsel Shri. Tekale placed reliance on some observations made by this Court at Nagpur Bench in Criminal Writ Petition No. 793/2019 (M/s. M.S.S. Foods and Processor Vs. The Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration, Mah. State and Ors.) decided on 4.9.2019.

entities.text: Criminal Writ Petition No. 793/2019 (M/s. M.S.S. Foods and Processor Vs. The Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration, Mah. State and Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It appears that at Nagpur Bench some interim order was made in this matter when similar point was raised.
It is already observed that before 4.9.2019 this point was decided and that decision is not refected in the interim order made at Nagpur Bench on 4.9.2019.
9) Before parting with the judgment, it needs to be observed that the matter was frst kept for hearing on 19.10.2020 and on that day Advocate Shri. Tekale was ready to argue the matter.
He was given time to go through the aforesaid decisions which were already delivered on the point and then the matter was adjourned to 3.11.2020.

On that day Shri. Takale started with the argument and when this Court expressed that in view of the decisions already rendered it was not possible to give diferent decision, Shri. Tekale submitted that his party wanted that one Advocate from Delhi should argue the matter.
Such approach and tactics cannot be tolerated and so, this Court took decision to decide the matter on the basis of aforesaid circumstances.
In the result, the following order.
ORDER The petition stands dismissed.

[ SHRIKANT D. KULKARNI, J.] [ T.V. NALAWADE, J.] ssc/
